A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a general framework for lexicographic compositions of multiple binary relations into one binary relation and have shown the conditions that the choice functions representing the two distinct procedures have to satisfy in order to be consistent with a number of choice consistency conditions.
, in general, the two procedures are not equivalent, and the outcomes of each depend on the order of application.

we have provided the conditions under which lexicographic procedures can be used to compose multiple criteria, and we have also identified the conditions under which these procedures are order-independent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice function representing the second procedure is more restrictive than the choice function representing first procedure.

there are many different ways to compose multiple criteria lexicographically and that each of these procedures has distinct conditions under which the outcomes are consistent with choice-consistency conditions and are independent of the lexicographic order of the criteria.

there is no single lexicographic composition procedure that is consistent under all possible choice-consistency conditions, nor is there one procedure that is consistent with the choice-consistency conditions and independent of the order in which the criteria are applied.
